summary: "One Last Time" is a song by Ariana Grande from her second studio album "My Everything", first released as a promotional single in 2014 and later sent to radio as the album's fifth and final single in February 2015. The note covers its writers, producers, French and Italian versions, and the found-footage-style music video directed with input from Max Landis, which features Victorious co-stars Matt Bennett and Elizabeth Gillies.
one_line: Ariana Grande's "One Last Time" was the fifth single from "My Everything", with a found-footage-style video and French and Italian versions.
key_facts: "One Last Time" was recorded by Ariana Grande for her second studio album "My Everything".
The song was written by David Guetta, Savan Kotecha, Giorgio Tuinfort, Rami Yacoub, and Carl Falk.
Rami Yacoub and Carl Falk produced the song, with Giorgio Tuinfort as co-producer and Ilya as co-producer and vocal producer.
"One Last Time" was first released on the iTunes Store on August 22, 2014 as the second promotional single from the album.
On February 10, 2015, the song was sent to contemporary hit radio as the fifth and final single from "My Everything".
A French version with Kendji Girac, titled "Attends-moi", was released on February 16, 2015 in France, Belgium and Switzerland and is on the deluxe version of Girac's album "Kendji" (2015).
An Italian version featuring rapper Fedez was released on May 26, 2015 only in Italy.
The music video was filmed in early January 2015 and stars Matt Bennett, Grande's co-star from the Nickelodeon sitcom Victorious.
Elizabeth Gillies, also from Victorious, was confirmed by Max Landis as one of the news reporter voices at the start of the video.
Max Landis revealed the single by tweeting that Earth would pass through the tail of the comet Eurydice in one week.
The lyric video was released on Grande's Vevo on February 6, 2015; a teaser was posted on Instagram on February 12, 2015.
The music video, presented as found footage similar to Landis' Chronicle, was released on February 15, 2015 on Vevo.
The video passed 100 million views on June 8, becoming Grande's sixth Vevo-certified video after "Love Me Harder".
